posture_tips: Set the seat so your armpits sit snug against the top edge of the preacher pad.
Keep the backs of your upper arms pressed into the pad for the whole set.
Curl the EZ-bar until your biceps are fully contracted, then lower over 2-3 seconds to just short of lockout.
Don't lift your elbows off the pad or roll your shoulders forward to finish the rep.
Never let the bar drop at the bottom; control the final stretch to spare your elbows.

name_es: Curl predicador con mancuerna (a una mano)
posture_tips: Rest your whole triceps on the pad with your armpit over the edge and the dumbbell palm-up.
Keep your shoulder down and torso still; use your free hand on the pad for stability.
Curl all the way up without lifting your arm, then lower slowly to just short of full extension.
Don't twist your torso or turn your wrist inward to finish the rep.
Pick a weight you can brake at the bottom; bouncing out of full extension loads the elbow hard.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your abs braced without leaning back.
Curl the dumbbells to shoulder height, then lower over 2-3 seconds to full extension.
Don't swing your body or drive your elbows forward to borrow momentum.
If you have to swing to get the weight up, go lighter and keep the reps clean.

name_es: Curl con mancuernas (de pie, agarre descentrado)
posture_tips: Grip each dumbbell with your pinky against the inner plate so more weight sits on the thumb side.
Keep your elbows fixed at your sides and your wrists neutral, not bent back.
Curl while rotating your palm up all the way, then lower slowly as you resist the rotation.
Don't relax the supination at the top; that extra twist is the whole point of the offset grip.
Go lighter than a regular curl; the offset grip puts more demand on your wrist.
Lie back on an incline bench, arms hanging, with your pinky against the inner plate.
Keep your back and head on the bench and your arms hanging straight down behind your torso.
Curl while turning your palm up without letting the elbow drift forward, then lower to a full stretch.
Don't peel your shoulders off the bench or bring your elbows forward as you curl.
Always lower under control; the biceps stretch in this position is intense.
Stand with dumbbells at your sides and your palms facing each other.
Keep your wrists straight and your elbows tucked against your body throughout.
Curl the dumbbell up to your shoulder like swinging a hammer, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't rotate your palm up or roll your shoulder forward as you curl.
Don't swing your torso; if your posture breaks down, reduce the weight.
Lie chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight toward the floor.
Keep your upper arms perpendicular to the floor and your palms facing each other all set.
Curl without moving your elbows, squeeze for a second at the top, and lower slowly.
Don't pull your elbows back or push them forward to gain range.
Plant your feet and chest firmly so the bench doesn't shift during the set.
Set the pulley low, grab the rope with palms facing each other, and take a step back.
Keep your elbows tucked to your torso and stand tall without leaning back.
Curl the rope to your chest, pulling the ends slightly apart, then lower under control.
Don't let the cable drag your elbows forward on the way down.
Keep tension on the cable at the end of the set and don't let the rope snap back.
Grip the bar underhand at shoulder width with your arms fully extended.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your torso doesn't arch backward.
Curl the bar in an arc to your chest without moving your elbows, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't hip-thrust the bar to get it moving off the bottom.
If a straight bar strains your wrists, switch to an EZ-bar.
Grip the EZ-bar on the inner or outer bends with your palms angled slightly inward.
Keep your chest up and your elbows just in front of your ribs.
Curl until the bar nears your chest, then lower to just short of full extension.
Don't shrug your shoulders or let your elbows ride up at the top.
Keep a neutral spine; don't lean back to cheat the weight up.
Set the bench to about 45-60 degrees, lie back, and let your arms hang with palms forward.
Keep your shoulders against the pad and your elbows pointing at the floor.
Curl without letting your elbows drift forward, then lower until your biceps are fully stretched.
Don't lift your head or shoulders off the bench as the set gets hard.
Start light; the stretched position puts a lot of load on the front of the shoulder.
Sit on a bench with legs apart and brace your triceps against your inner thigh.
Keep your torso leaned forward and still, with your free hand on your other knee.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, turning your pinky up, then lower slowly.
Don't use your leg or torso to push the dumbbell up.
Lower to just short of lockout without letting the weight drop at the end.
Set the pulley low, grab the straight bar palms-up, and stand close to the stack.
Keep your elbows at your sides, torso tall, and knees slightly bent.
Curl the bar to your chest, squeeze for a second, and lower against the cable's pull.
Don't stand too far from the pulley; the cable will pull your elbows forward.
Return the bar to the stack under control when you finish; don't just let go.
Face away from a low pulley, grab the handle, and step forward with your arm trailing behind you.
Keep your upper arm behind your torso and your chest open on every rep.
Curl all the way up without letting your arm drift forward, then return slowly to the stretch.
Don't bring your elbow forward as you curl; you lose the stretch this exercise is built on.
Use a stable split stance so the cable can't pull you off balance.
Adjust the seat so your elbow lines up with the machine's pivot point.
Keep your arms on the pad and your chest in contact with the support.
Curl the handles to a full contraction and lower over 2-3 seconds without losing tension.
Don't lift your hips off the seat to grind out the last reps.
Don't let the weight stack slam at the bottom; control your elbow extension.
Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width with your arms fully extended.
Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms throughout.
Curl the bar up to your chest by bending your elbows, then lower it slowly.
Don't let your wrists bend down as fatigue sets in.
Use less weight than a regular curl; the overhand grip limits how much you can handle safely.
Set the pulley high, grab the rope with palms facing each other, and bring your elbows to your sides.
Keep your chest up, a slight forward lean, and your elbows locked in beside your ribs.
Push down and spread the rope ends apart at the bottom, then return under control.
Don't let your elbows flare or drift forward as the rope comes back up.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to take strain off your neck.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps en polea (barra V)
posture_tips: Set the pulley high, grab the V-bar, and start with your elbows bent at your sides.
Keep your wrists straight and your torso braced with a slight forward lean.
Extend to full lockout without snapping, then come up until your forearms pass parallel.
Don't lean over the bar to push it down with your bodyweight.
Plant your feet firmly and apart so heavy loads don't pull you off balance.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps sobre la cabeza en polea (cuerda)
posture_tips: Face away from the pulley, hold the rope behind your head, and stagger your feet.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head for the whole set.
Extend your elbows up and forward, then return slowly until you feel the stretch.
Don't let your elbows flare out or your lower back arch.
Brace your abs to protect your lower back while the cable pulls you backward.
Lie on a flat bench holding the EZ-bar over your shoulders with arms extended.
Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling, angled slightly back toward your head.
Lower the bar toward your forehead or behind your head by bending only your elbows, then press back up.
Don't flare your elbows or let the movement turn into a press.
Use a spotter or a weight you fully control; the bar passes close to your face.
Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, arms extended.
Keep your upper arms fixed and parallel to each other throughout.
Lower the dumbbells beside your head by bending your elbows, then extend back to the top.
Don't let the dumbbells drift apart or your elbows flare as you press up.
Lower slowly and keep a firm grip so you don't hit your head.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps sobre la cabeza con mancuerna (sentado)
posture_tips: Sit on a bench with back support and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Keep your back on the pad, ribs down, and elbows pointing forward.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head until you feel a stretch, then extend your elbows.
Don't arch your lower back when the dumbbell is overhead.
Cup the top plate firmly with both palms so the dumbbell can't slip.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps sobre la cabeza con mancuerna (a una mano)
posture_tips: Hold the dumbbell overhead with one arm extended, seated or standing with your abs braced.
Keep your elbow pointing at the ceiling and close to your head; your other hand can support it.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending the elbow, then extend fully again.
Don't let your elbow drift out or your torso lean to one side.
Work with a light weight you control; the dumbbell travels behind your head.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps sobre la cabeza con barra Z
posture_tips: Take a close grip on the EZ-bar and press it overhead with your arms extended.
Keep your elbows narrow and pointing forward, with your ribs down.
Lower the bar behind your head to a stretch, then extend without moving your upper arms.
Don't compensate on the way up by arching your back or flaring your elbows.
Do it seated with back support if your lower back arches when standing.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps en polea (barra recta)
posture_tips: Set the pulley high and grab the straight bar overhand at shoulder width.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your wrists in line with your forearms.
Push the bar down to full elbow extension, then let it rise to chest height.
Don't let the bar come up past your chest or your elbows leave your sides.
Hold a stable stance with knees slightly bent so you don't rock.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps en polea (agarre supino)
posture_tips: Set the pulley high and grab the bar palms-up at shoulder width.
Keep your elbows by your torso and your wrists firm, not bent back.
Extend your elbows all the way down, squeeze your triceps, and return slowly to 90 degrees.
Don't roll your shoulders forward to squeeze out the last reps.
Use less weight than with an overhand grip to avoid overloading your wrists.

name_es: Extensión de tríceps en polea (a una mano)
posture_tips: Set the pulley high with a single handle and hold it with your elbow tucked to your side.
Keep your shoulders level and your torso square to the pulley without twisting.
Extend your elbow fully, then return under control until your forearm passes parallel.
Don't let your elbow drift away from your body or your shoulder roll forward.
Rest your free hand on the machine to stay balanced.
Place one hand and knee on the bench with a flat back and the dumbbell in your other hand.
Keep your upper arm parallel to the floor and your elbow tucked to your side all set.
Extend your elbow until your arm is straight, squeeze for a second, and return slowly.
Don't let your elbow drop as you extend or swing the dumbbell with momentum.
Keep your spine neutral and don't rotate your torso as your arm moves.
Set the pulley low, hold the cable bare or with a handle, and hinge your torso forward.
Keep your upper arm tight to your body and parallel to the floor with a flat back.
Extend your elbow back to lockout, then return slowly without losing tension.
Don't move your shoulder or upper arm; only your forearm should move.
Brace your free hand on the machine to keep your back stable.
Lie on a flat bench with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder width.
Keep your elbows pointing toward your feet and your shoulder blades set on the bench.
Lower the bar toward your upper chest or chin by bending your elbows, then press back up.
Don't turn it into a bench press; the bar shouldn't touch your chest.
Use safety arms or a spotter; the bar comes down close to your face.
Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot and rest your arms on the pad.
Keep your back against the pad and your shoulders down throughout the set.
Extend your elbows fully, squeeze your triceps, and return slowly into flexion.
Don't lift your elbows off the pad to push with your shoulders.
Don't let the stack slam on the way back; control the entire eccentric.
Sit with your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up.
Keep your forearms fixed with only your wrists hanging over the edge.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl your wrists up as high as you can.
Don't lift your forearms or use your biceps to move the bar.
Stick to moderate weight and high reps to look after your wrists.

name_es: Curl de muñeca inverso con barra
posture_tips: Rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms down, with your wrists over the edge.
Keep your forearms glued to the support and your fingers wrapped firmly around the bar.
Raise the backs of your hands as high as possible, then lower slowly into the stretch.
Don't move your elbows or swing the bar to gain range.
Start very light; your forearm extensors fatigue quickly.
Pick up two heavy dumbbells from the floor with a neutral spine and stand tall.
Keep your shoulders down and back, chest up, and arms straight at your sides.
Squeeze the handles hard and hold the position for the set time without moving.
Don't shrug your shoulders or let the dumbbells swing.
When finished, lower the dumbbells by bending your hips and knees, not by rounding your back.
Hang from the bar with a firm grip, arms straight, and legs together.
Keep your shoulders engaged and your body still; kill any swing before you start.
Raise your straight legs while curling your pelvis up, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't use momentum from swinging to get your legs up.
If you can't control the swing yet, start with hanging knee raises.
Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead.
Keep your legs together and your arms in line with your ears as you rise.
Lift your torso and legs together to touch your feet, then lower slowly without collapsing.
Don't yank on your neck or bend your knees to reach the top.
Keep your lower back controlled on the way down; if it arches, shorten the range.
Set your forearms down with elbows under shoulders and extend your legs onto your toes.
Hold a straight line from head to heels with your glutes squeezed.
Hold the position, breathing steadily and pushing the floor away with your forearms.
Don't let your hips sag or pike up toward the ceiling.
End the set once you lose alignment, even if the timer isn't up.
Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and feet stacked or staggered.
Keep your hips, shoulders, and ankles in one straight line.
Lift your hips off the floor and hold without rotating your torso.
Don't let your hips drop or shift backward.
Drop to your bottom knee if you can't hold the line with straight legs.
Lie on your back with arms reaching to the ceiling and hips and knees at 90 degrees.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor for the entire exercise.
Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg, then return before switching sides.
Don't let your lower back peel off the floor as your leg extends.
Shorten the leg reach if you can't keep your back flat.
Get on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your back flat and pelvis level, as if balancing a glass on it.
Reach the opposite arm and leg out to horizontal, pause, and return slowly.
Don't arch your lower back or rotate your hips as your leg lifts.
Move slowly and deliberately; stability matters more than height.
Kneel facing a high pulley and hold the rope beside your head.
Keep your hips still and high; the movement should come from your spine.
Curl your torso down, bringing your elbows toward your thighs, then return against the cable.
Don't sit back on your heels or pull the weight down with your arms.
Pick a weight that lets you flex your spine smoothly without jerking.
Kneel on a mat and hold the wheel under your shoulders with straight arms.
Keep your pelvis tucked and your ribs down throughout the rollout.
Roll forward as far as you can control, then pull back using your abs.
Don't let your lower back sag as the wheel moves away from your knees.
Increase your range gradually; start with short rollouts.
Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width grip and your legs relaxed.
Keep your shoulders engaged and your body steady without swinging.
Bring your knees toward your chest while tilting your pelvis up, then lower slowly.
Don't stop at knees to 90 degrees without curling your pelvis up.
Drop off the bar under control if your grip gives out before your abs do.
Stand side-on to a chest-height pulley and hold the handle against your sternum.
Keep feet hip-width, knees soft, and shoulders square to the front.
Press your arms straight out while resisting the twist, hold two seconds, and return to your chest.
Don't let your torso rotate toward the pulley as you press out.
Step away from the pulley only as far as you can resist rotation with good posture.
Set the pulley high, stand side-on, and grip the handle with both hands above your shoulder.
Keep your arms nearly straight and rotate from your torso with your hips following.
Pull the handle diagonally toward the opposite knee, then control the rotation back.
Don't pull with just your arms or bend your elbows to move the cable.
Pivot your back foot as you rotate to keep stress off your knee and lower back.
Sit with knees bent, lean your torso back, and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Keep your spine long and chest up without slouching.
Rotate side to side under control, bringing your hands beside each hip.
Don't just move your arms; the twist should come from your ribcage.
Keep your heels on the floor if lifting your feet costs you your back position.
Hook your feet on the decline bench and lie back with your hands crossed on your chest.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and your neck relaxed.
Curl up one vertebra at a time, then lower slowly until you almost touch the bench.
Don't pull on your head with your hands or throw yourself up with momentum.
Choose a decline you can control on the way down before adding weight.
Lie on your back with arms overhead and legs together and extended.
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor and your shoulders lifted.
Raise your arms and legs a few inches and hold the banana shape while breathing.
Don't let your lower back arch as your legs lower.
Bend your knees or raise your legs higher if you can't keep your lower back down.
Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keep your hips low and stable as you alternate legs.
Drive one knee toward your chest and switch legs at a steady rhythm.
Don't let your hips pike up as you speed up.
Slow down if your shoulders start drifting off your hands.
Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands beside your temples.
Keep your neck neutral, with a fist's width of space between chin and chest.
Lift your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs, then lower slowly.
Don't pull on your head with your hands to get up.
Exhale as you rise and don't hold your breath during the set.
Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your glutes or at your sides.
Keep your lower back in contact with the floor at all times.
Raise your legs to vertical, then lower them slowly without touching the floor.
Don't arch your back as your legs approach the floor.
Bend your knees slightly if your lower back lifts off the floor.
Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand with a neutral spine and stand tall.
Keep your shoulders back, chest up, and eyes forward as you walk.
Walk the set distance with short, firm steps without stopping.
Don't lean forward or let your shoulders round.
Clear your path of obstacles and set the weights down by bending your hips and knees.
Hold a single dumbbell at one side like a suitcase, arm straight.
Keep your shoulders level and torso upright without leaning toward the weight.
Walk the set distance at a controlled pace, then repeat on the other side.
Don't compensate by leaning away from the dumbbell.
Start with a moderate weight; lateral stability is what you're training.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell a step in front of you.
Keep a neutral spine and hinge at the hips on every rep; this is not a squat.
Hike the bell between your legs and snap your hips through to send it to chest height.
Don't lift the bell with your arms or lean back at the top.
Clear the space around you and park the kettlebell on the floor under control when done.
Hold the dumbbells at your shoulders, elbows forward, feet hip-width apart.
Keep your chest up and your torso braced through the squat.
Squat down, then drive up and use the leg drive to press the dumbbells overhead.
Don't split the squat and press into two moves; it should be one continuous motion.
Lock out overhead with your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Keep your body in line in the plank, hips neither sagging nor piked.
Squat, jump back to a plank, do a push-up, jump your feet to your hands, and jump up.
Don't land stiff-legged or let your chest crash to the floor.
Land softly with bent knees and slow down if your form slips.
Set up with the bar over your midfoot, feet hip-width, grip just outside your legs.
Keep a neutral spine and the bar close to your body through the entire pull.
Drive your hips and knees to full extension and catch the bar on your shoulders, elbows forward.
Don't pull with your arms before your hips have fully extended.
Learn the lift light or with a coach, and use bumper plates that can be dropped.
Lie on your back holding the kettlebell in one hand, arm vertical, same-side knee bent.
Keep your arm locked and your eyes on the kettlebell throughout the get-up.
Rise in stages: elbow, hand, bridge, knee, stand; reverse the steps in order to come down.
Don't rush the transitions or let your arm tilt off vertical.
Practice first with no weight or a shoe balanced on your fist before loading the kettlebell.
Hook your feet under the decline bench pad and press the dumbbells up over your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms angled slightly back toward your head and still for the whole set.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your ears, then extend until your arms are straight.
Don't let your elbows flare out or turn the rep into a press by moving your upper arms.
Hand the dumbbells off or bring them to your chest before sitting up; never sit up with arms extended.
Lie head-up on a decline bench and grip the bench behind your head with knees bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your lower back pressed into the pad and your head resting on the bench.
Curl your hips up and toward your chest until they leave the pad, then lower them slowly.
Don't swing your legs or use momentum to flip your hips up.
Start with a gentle decline and only steepen it once you can control every rep.
Hook your feet on the decline bench and hold a plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and your lower back close to the pad.
Curl your shoulders up until your abs are fully shortened, then lower until your shoulder blades touch.
Don't sit all the way up; stop before your torso is upright so the abs stay loaded.
Add weight only when you can lower every rep slowly without straining your neck.
